summary: Interleaved tenant burst causing GPU serialization and request timeouts in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports widespread p95/p99 latency regressions and request timeouts from their dedicated reservation in us-west. Impact started as intermittent 504s during peak traffic and escalated to sustained tail latency increases (~x10 p95) for inference endpoints.

Impact:
- Multiple customer services saw increased latency and 504 timeouts across both short and long sequence requests.
- Errors observed by customer: upstream 504 (gateway timeout) and client-observed hang > 60s.
- Affects critical production traffic for Fathom Analytics (dedicated reservation).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: res-44-usw-gpu (8xA100-slices, mixed tenancy).
- Runtime version: realtime-runner v2.18.3
- Autoscaler config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, scale_cooldown=120s, cpu_threshold=0.6
- Models in rotation: rw/open-owl-7b-v2 (primary), compat/13b-quant-lite (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Replay burst traffic pattern: 1400 rps sustained for ~60s composed of mixed short/long sequences (mean tokens 50, 5% long > 1200 tokens).
2) Observe p95 and p99 climb and requests start timing out between 30-90s.
3) Rolling back to smaller batch size or reducing concurrency mitigates for customer.

Observed behavior:
- Serving runtime shows intervals of GPU kernel serialization where multiple tenant jobs cannot overlap kernels, resulting in head-of-line blocking.
- Autoscaler did not increase replicas fast enough; observed queue-depth growth on the scheduler leading to request queueing.
- High GPU memory churn/evictions coincident with background batch jobs.

Expected behavior:
- Serving runtime should maintain steady p95/p99 with autoscaler scaling to absorb burst without long tail latencies or 504s.

Logs / Metrics / Links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DEDICATED/res-44-usw-gpu-overview
- Recent trace sample: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0b9a2c
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p1645
- Kernel scheduling spikes: prometheus query cpu:kernel_serialize_seconds{pool="res-44-usw"}

Customer notes:
- Customer temporarily reduced client concurrency and saw immediate latency improvements.
- Customer requests root cause and long-term mitigation (isolation, autoscale tuning, or reservation sizing).

2026-03-11 02:18 - Support (Aisha Kaur): Customer confirmed that pinning model to rw/open-owl-7b-v2 still showed slowdowns; switching to smaller batch_size=4 improved tail latency.
2026-03-12 15:30 - Mateo Chen: Applied temporary scheduler throttling to limit concurrent background batch jobs on res-44-usw. Request queue depth started decreasing within 5 minutes.
2026-03-13 09:50 - Customer (Fathom Analytics - Jorge Ramos): After the throttling change we observed reduced 504s. Requesting permanent fix and SLA assurance.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 12:00 - Hypothesis 1: Noisy tenant burst created large kernel serialization windows on GPUs (kernel mutual exclusion in runtime). Evidence: kernel_serialize_seconds spike aligned with customer errors.

2026-03-10 13:30 - Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler cooldown/config too conservative (min_replicas=2) caused underprovision during burst; scale up lag ~45-90s. Evidence: horizontal_scaling_events log shows scale up started after queue depth crossed 8k.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Hypothesis 3: Background batch jobs with large sequence lengths triggered VRAM paging and preemption, evicting KV caches and causing recompile/rehydration delays. Observed GPU memory_pressure and pagefault counters rising.
2026-03-11 10:05 - Reproduction: Ran synthetic mixed workload in staging against res-44-usw-sim. Reproduced p95 jump when interleaving long-seq batch jobs from another tenant at 20% of total RPS.

2026-03-12 14:00 - Root cause (working theory): Combined effect of tenant interleaving (noisy bursts), kernel scheduling serialization, and autoscaler mis-sizing led to head-of-line blocking and then queued request timeouts.
resolution:
Workaround applied and permanent actions planned:

Immediate mitigation (done):
- Throttled non-critical background batch jobs on res-44-usw to reduce interleaved kernel contention.
- Increased scheduler soft limits to reduce per-tenant max concurrent batches for mixed-tenancy pools.
- Customer instructed to temporarily lower batch_size/concurrency for critical endpoints.

Short-term fix (next 48-72h):
- Adjust autoscaler: reduce scale_cooldown to 30s, increase min_replicas to 4 for res-44-usw reservation, and add burst_scale policy to pre-warm nodes when queue depth increases rapidly. PR: https://github.com/redwood-infer/autoscaler/pull/198
- Add targeted eviction protection for small latency-sensitive jobs so they are prioritized over background batches in mixed pools.

Long-term remediation (roadmap):
- Implement tenant-aware admission control to avoid interleaved kernel serialization in mixed pools; scheduling work tracked in INT-3301.
- Offer stronger isolation options (dedicated-slice-per-tenant) as part of Dedicated product for enterprise customers.

Post-incident follow-ups:
- Postmortem scheduled: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/postmortems/SUP-563210 (owner: Mateo Chen).
- Customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-16.

Status: Mitigations deployed; monitoring shows p95 back within acceptable range for now. Keeping ticket open for completion of autoscaler changes and postmortem.
